# AI Working Log

A running log of what I built each session, what decisions I made, and what's left. Submitted as part of the 8x contest entry.

---

## Day 1 — May 6, 2026 · Scaffold

- Forked `8xsocial/template-webapp` → `Anuj7411/metric-fyi`. Cloned locally, ran `pnpm install`.
- Stripped the template's SaaS demo content: `CANDIDATE_ASSIGNMENT.md`, `app/upgrade`, `app/profile`, `app/privacy`, `app/terms`, `app/api/account`, `contexts/subscription-context.tsx`, the subscriptions migration, `lib/colors.ts`, `lib/confetti.ts`, and all 11 `8x`-branded favicons / web-app-manifest images.
- Wired the Lab Lime token system into `app/globals.css` via Tailwind v4's `@theme` directive — every color, surface, and font variable from the design bundle's `palette.jsx` and `index.html` is now a CSS custom property.
- Self-hosted `ClashDisplay-Variable.ttf` from the design bundle into `public/fonts/`. Loaded via `next/font/local` with a `200 700` axis range. Geist Sans + Geist Mono added via the official `geist` npm package.
- Replaced `app/layout.tsx`, `app/page.tsx`, `components/navigation.tsx`, `components/footer.tsx`, and `app/not-found.tsx` with stripped METRIC.fyi shells. Homepage shows the locked headline, a disabled placeholder input, and a live-indicator chip — the real upload pipeline lands Day 3.
- Removed `AuthProvider` from `layout.tsx` for now — re-adds Day 8. Reason: the bundled Supabase client init throws if env vars are missing, and the homepage shouldn't depend on auth being wired.

### Decisions made today

- **Skipping local Supabase / Docker** in favor of Supabase cloud. Faster to set up, identical for our purposes, no Windows admin friction.
- **Skipping social URL ingestion** for V1 — Vercel serverless can't run yt-dlp cleanly and platforms actively block scraping. File upload + 3 pre-loaded sample videos gets reviewers to the magic moment in <30 seconds.
- **Section-by-section streaming** (4 small Gemini calls in sequence) instead of one giant streamed-JSON object — more reliable, easier to recover when one section fails, perceived as faster.
- **TBJ Moder swapped for Geist Italic.** TBJ Moder ships with the design bundle as a *demo* version, which isn't licensed for production. Going with Geist + Geist Italic across body and editorial callouts.

### Pushback I committed to

- App stays dark; the public `/r/[id]` report screen flips to paper. The report is designed to screenshot well in white Twitter feeds; a dark dashboard screenshot vanishes there.
- No marketing scroll below the landing hero. The page ends at the input.

### Mid-session — AI logs restructure

- Contest spec ([8xengineer.com/guidelines/ai-logs](https://8xengineer.com/guidelines/ai-logs)) expects `/ai-logs/` folder, not a root-level file.
- Moved `AI_LOG.md` → `ai-logs/SUMMARY.md`. Copied raw Claude Code transcript as `ai-logs/*.jsonl` (accepted format).
- Added `pnpm logs:sync` (wraps `scripts/sync-logs.sh`) — idempotent re-sync before commits.

---

## Day 2 — May 14, 2026 · Visual system + working hero

- Installed `framer-motion` (locked-stack animation lib).
- Wrote `lib/motion.ts` — single source of truth for easings, durations, stagger. Lifted directly from the design's `motion.jsx`: `[0.2,0.8,0.2,1]` cubic-bezier, durations 120/220/480ms, 40ms stagger, 1400ms score count-up. Forbidden: bounce, spring overshoot, parallax.
- Wrote `lib/sample-videos.ts` — typed metadata for the 3 demo clips (`@khaby.lame`, `@itsmaya`, `@bento.mufc`). Day 3 plugs real mp4 URLs in.
- Built `components/marketing/Logo.tsx` (lime square + mono wordmark, reused by nav and future report pages).
- Rewrote `components/ui/button.tsx` from scratch — replaced shadcn's 6 stock variants with our 2: `signal` (lime fill on ink) and `ghost` (line border, dim text). Square corners (matches design), no shadow, mono caps with `0.1em` tracking.
- Built `components/landing/UploadCard.tsx` — page-wide HTML5 drag-and-drop (no `react-dropzone` dep), 100MB limit, accepts `.mp4/.mov/.webm`, dim cursor when empty, lime border + "drop to upload →" when dragging.
- Built `components/landing/SampleVideoPicker.tsx` — 3 chips, active state (lime border) when one's picked.
- Built `components/landing/Hero.tsx` — composes headline + upload card + sample picker + receipt-style stats block. Staggered Framer reveals on mount. Picked-state lifted here so the score button enables/disables.
- Refactored `app/page.tsx` to a thin shell: `Navigation + Hero + Footer`.
- Updated `Navigation` to use the new `Logo` component.

### Cleanups while wiring

- Deleted unused stock shadcn primitives (`alert-dialog`, `sidebar`, `sheet`, `input`, `separator`, `skeleton`, `tooltip`, `select`, `card`, `label`). They referenced variants our new `Button` doesn't have. Only `button.tsx` remains in `components/ui/`. We'll re-add fresh primitives with brand styling as needed Days 5+.

### Decisions made today

- **Page-wide drag-drop** instead of just on the input row. Forgiving UX: drop anywhere → it lands on the input.
- **Score button enables on file pick OR sample pick.** Clicking shows a toast saying "Day 3 wires this up" — keeps the demo honest about scope.
- **No "Pricing" nav link.** Brief skips payments; nav items now read `How it works · Examples · Sign in →`.

### What's left

- Day 3: upload pipeline, Supabase Storage, `reports` table with RLS (**requires Supabase project — user creating now**)
- Day 4: Gemini 2.0 Flash analysis backend + the prompt
- Day 5: streaming reveal + report layout
- Day 6: visible reasoning (citations) + video player coupling
- Days 7–10: shareable report, auth + history, mobile + perf, Loom + submit

content.text:
Strong opinion: **don't change the direction.** Here's why, and then where you're actually right.

## Why context.dev's look is wrong for us

That site is for SEO/AI-visibility audits — sold to marketers and dev relations folks. Light/serif/teal reads as "research report," which fits *that* product. Our audience lives in CapCut, Premiere, DaVinci, TikTok's editor — every tool they use is dark. A light dashboard for video creators reads like Mailchimp wandered into the wrong room. The design direction you locked in with the design assistant was explicitly: *"the analytical precision of a Bloomberg terminal, dressed in the cultural language of a creator's For You page"* — dark, dense, instrument-like. We considered + rejected lighter/warmer palettes (Cinema, Cyber Cottage) during the design phase. If we flip to light now we're chasing a vibe that fights our positioning.

## But you're not wrong that the page feels empty

It is. Below the input bar there's just void. The grid background is set to ~4% opacity (barely visible), the receipt-block bottom-right is small and easy to miss, and there's no preview of *what* you'll get back. Without motion, the screenshot looks like 80% black with one big sentence on it. That's not "minimalist" — that's underdesigned.

## What I'd actually fix (3 specific things, ~45 min total)

1. **Stronger grid** — drop the cell size from 120px → 88px (matches the design bundle), bump line opacity from 8% → 14%. Suddenly the page reads as "instrument," not "loading screen." Free, just a CSS tweak.

2. **Sample-output preview card** under the input — a small dashed-bordered slab showing `SCORE: ── · HOOK: ── · PACING: ── · CAPTION: ──` with placeholder dashes that flip to numbers if you hover. Hints at the deliverable without spoiling it. Solves the "what does this give me?" emptiness.

3. **Corner crosshairs** at the four corners of the viewport (the design prototype uses these in `cover.jsx`). Tiny `+` marks. Reads as "this is a measurement instrument," ties to the Bloomberg-terminal thesis. ~10 lines of CSS.

All three preserve the direction. None of them touch the color palette. Total work: ~45 minutes, one commit.

## Two options

- **A. Polish now, then Day 3.** I do the 3 fixes above, commit, then start Day 3 (upload pipeline) in the same session.
- **B. Stick to the plan — defer polish to Day 9.** Day 9 is explicitly the "mobile + perf + polish" day. Doing it then means we polish with full context of every screen, not just the landing.

My recommendation: **A.** The empty landing is the first thing every reviewer + judge sees, and you'll be sharing this URL on Twitter/the contest form long before Day 9. Fixing it now also un-blocks you from posting it publicly. Day 9 polish budget then goes to the report screen and mobile pass.

---

## Also still need from you to actually start Day 3

You confirmed migration path **B (Supabase CLI)** — good, I'll set that up. But two items still gating Day 3:

1. **Service-role key** — Settings → API → `service_role` secret. Paste it here. Needed for the server upload endpoint to bypass Storage RLS.
2. **Confirm you have the DB password saved** somewhere — you set it when creating the Supabase project. `supabase db push` will prompt for it once.

Reply with: (A or B for polish) + the service-role key + "yes I have the DB password." I execute.

content.text:
Honest answer: **yes, anon-only is fine and arguably better.** You're correct.

Anon + properly-configured RLS forces us to write the security policy explicitly, which is the *right* pattern. Service-role bypasses all RLS — one bug in server code leaks everything. For contest judges, "anon + RLS policies" is a stronger engineering signal than "service-role and trust ourselves." Past projects of yours that worked with just anon were doing this correctly.

The Day 3 flow without service-role:

1. Client picks file → POST `/api/upload/init`
2. Server (using anon key) inserts a `reports` row → returns `{ id, storagePath }`
3. Client uploads file directly to Supabase Storage with anon key
4. Client navigates to `/r/[id]`

All three steps work with anon key as long as RLS allows:
- `reports` INSERT for `anon` role (with column-level CHECK constraints — no `user_id`, status must be `pending`, etc.)
- Storage INSERT for `anon` role into the `videos` bucket (with file-size limit enforced at bucket level)
- `reports` SELECT for `anon` role only when filtering by exact id (no list/enumerate)

Cleaner, more secure, exactly the right pattern.

**Scratch the service-role ask entirely.** We don't need it Day 3 or beyond.

2. **Confirm you have the Supabase DB password saved.** Needed for `supabase db push` to prompt-and-apply. You set it when creating the project. Yes/no — don't paste it here.

-- METRIC.fyi · reports table
-- Created Day 3 (2026-05-14)
--
-- A `report` is one analysis run: one uploaded video → one virality score
-- and one breakdown. Anonymous users can create reports (no auth required —
-- the contest's "no-signup demo path" is non-negotiable). Authenticated
-- users (Day 8) can claim/save reports to their history by setting user_id.
--
-- Security model:
--   - Anon role can INSERT only with status='pending' and user_id IS NULL.
--   - Anon role CANNOT directly SELECT — all reads go through the
--     fetch_report() SECURITY DEFINER function, which enforces "id is a UUID
--     and you must know it." Standard public-by-unguessable-link pattern.
--   - Service role (Vercel deploy) is not used; everything runs under anon
--     + RLS, which is the more secure pattern.

create extension if not exists "pgcrypto"; -- for gen_random_uuid()

create table if not exists public.reports (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),

  -- Pipeline state. Day 4 transitions pending → analyzing → ready (or failed).
  status text not null default 'pending'
    check (status in ('pending', 'analyzing', 'ready', 'failed')),

  -- Where the file lives in Storage (videos bucket). Set on insert.
  storage_path text not null,
  file_name text not null,
  file_size bigint not null
    check (file_size > 0 and file_size <= 104857600), -- 100 MiB hard cap
  mime_type text not null
    check (mime_type in ('video/mp4', 'video/quicktime', 'video/webm')),

  -- Filled by analysis pipeline (Day 4).
  duration_seconds numeric,
  analysis jsonb,
  error_message text,

  -- Ownership. Null = anonymous demo report. Day 8 lets signed-in users claim.
  user_id uuid references auth.users(id) on delete set null,

  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

-- updated_at auto-bump trigger
create or replace function public.tg_reports_set_updated_at()
returns trigger language plpgsql as $$
begin
  new.updated_at = now();
  return new;
end;
$$;

drop trigger if exists tg_reports_updated_at on public.reports;
create trigger tg_reports_updated_at
  before update on public.reports
  for each row execute function public.tg_reports_set_updated_at();

-- Enable RLS — every table gets it from day one.
alter table public.reports enable row level security;

-- Anon can INSERT a pending report, but cannot claim a user_id or seed
-- analysis data. The pipeline writes the rest later via the same RLS-bypassing
-- pattern (Day 4 will need a SECURITY DEFINER function for status updates).
drop policy if exists "anon insert pending" on public.reports;
create policy "anon insert pending" on public.reports
  for insert to anon
  with check (
    user_id is null
    and status = 'pending'
    and analysis is null
    and error_message is null
  );

-- Authenticated users can also create reports (own them by setting user_id).
drop policy if exists "authenticated insert own" on public.reports;
create policy "authenticated insert own" on public.reports
  for insert to authenticated
  with check (
    user_id = auth.uid()
    and status = 'pending'
    and analysis is null
    and error_message is null
  );

-- Authenticated users can SELECT their own reports (Day 8 — /history).
drop policy if exists "authenticated select own" on public.reports;
create policy "authenticated select own" on public.reports
  for select to authenticated
  using (user_id = auth.uid());

-- Note: NO direct SELECT policy for anon. They must use fetch_report().

-- Fetch a report by id. The only way anon clients read reports.
-- security definer = runs as table owner, bypassing RLS within the function.
-- The function itself filters by id, so callers can only get reports they
-- know the (unguessable v4) UUID for.
create or replace function public.fetch_report(p_id uuid)
returns public.reports
language sql stable
security definer
set search_path = public
as $$
  select * from public.reports where id = p_id limit 1;
$$;

revoke all on function public.fetch_report(uuid) from public;
grant execute on function public.fetch_report(uuid) to anon, authenticated;

-- Indexes
create index if not exists idx_reports_user_id on public.reports(user_id) where user_id is not null;
create index if not exists idx_reports_created_at on public.reports(created_at desc);

comment on table public.reports is
  'Virality analysis runs. Anon-creatable, anon-readable by id only (via fetch_report). Day 8 layers auth/history on top.';

-- security definer = runs as table owner, bypassing RLS within the function.
-- The function itself filters by id, so callers can only get reports they
-- know the (unguessable v4) UUID for.
create or replace function public.fetch_report(p_id uuid)
returns public.reports
language sql stable
security definer
set search_path = public
as $$
  select * from public.reports where id = p_id limit 1;
$$;

revoke all on function public.fetch_report(uuid) from public;
grant execute on function public.fetch_report(uuid) to anon, authenticated;

-- Indexes
create index if not exists idx_reports_user_id on public.reports(user_id) where user_id is not null;
create index if not exists idx_reports_created_at on public.reports(created_at desc);

comment on table public.reports is
  'Virality analysis runs. Anon-creatable, anon-readable by id only (via fetch_report). Day 8 layers auth/history on top.';

-- METRIC.fyi · Storage bucket for uploaded videos
-- Created Day 3 (2026-05-14)
--
-- One bucket: `videos`. Public-read (so the report page can use a plain
-- <video src> without signed URLs), anon-write (so the no-signup demo
-- path works), 100 MiB cap, mime-type restricted.
--
-- Same security model as the reports table: relies on unguessable UUIDs
-- for the storage path (we use the report's UUID as the filename),
-- so URLs aren't enumerable.

insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types)
values (
  'videos',
  'videos',
  true,                                              -- public-read by URL
  104857600,                                         -- 100 MiB
  array['video/mp4', 'video/quicktime', 'video/webm']
)
on conflict (id) do update set
  public = excluded.public,
  file_size_limit = excluded.file_size_limit,
  allowed_mime_types = excluded.allowed_mime_types;

-- Storage RLS policies (separate from table RLS)
-- Allow anyone (anon, authenticated) to upload to the videos bucket.
-- The actual size/mime checks are enforced by the bucket config above.
drop policy if exists "anon upload to videos" on storage.objects;
create policy "anon upload to videos"
  on storage.objects for insert
  to anon, authenticated
  with check (bucket_id = 'videos');

-- Public read access (matches `public = true` above, but the policy is
-- still required for PostgREST queries against storage.objects).
drop policy if exists "public read videos" on storage.objects;
create policy "public read videos"
  on storage.objects for select
  to public
  using (bucket_id = 'videos');

/**
 * Canonical Zod schemas for the report pipeline.
 * Single source of truth — used by API routes (request/response validation)
 * and by client code (response parsing, types).
 */
import { z } from "zod"

export const ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES = [
  "video/mp4",
  "video/quicktime",
  "video/webm",
] as const

export const MAX_BYTES = 104_857_600 // 100 MiB

export const ReportStatus = z.enum([
  "pending",
  "analyzing",
  "ready",
  "failed",
])
export type ReportStatus = z.infer<typeof ReportStatus>

/* ── /api/upload/init ─────────────────────────────────────────── */

export const UploadInitRequest = z.object({
  fileName: z.string().min(1).max(255),
  fileSize: z.number().int().positive().max(MAX_BYTES),
  mimeType: z.enum(ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES),
})
export type UploadInitRequest = z.infer<typeof UploadInitRequest>

export const UploadInitResponse = z.object({
  id: z.string().uuid(),
  storagePath: z.string(),
})
export type UploadInitResponse = z.infer<typeof UploadInitResponse>

/* ── Stored row (matches DB columns) ──────────────────────────── */

export const ReportRow = z.object({
  id: z.string().uuid(),
  status: ReportStatus,
  storage_path: z.string(),
  file_name: z.string(),
  file_size: z.number().int(),
  mime_type: z.string(),
  duration_seconds: z.number().nullable(),
  analysis: z.unknown().nullable(),
  error_message: z.string().nullable(),
  user_id: z.string().uuid().nullable(),
  created_at: z.string(),
  updated_at: z.string(),
})
export type ReportRow = z.infer<typeof ReportRow>

## Day 3 — May 14, 2026 · Upload pipeline + RLS

- Installed Supabase CLI as devDep. Wired three scripts: `pnpm db:link` (one-time link to `kjqwjilhxzeqkdydtsoj`), `pnpm db:push` (apply migrations), `pnpm db:types` (generate TypeScript types — Day 4+).
- Updated `supabase/config.toml`: `project_id = "metric-fyi"`, storage `file_size_limit = "100MiB"`.
- Wrote `supabase/migrations/20260514010000_create_reports.sql` — `reports` table with strict status/mime/size CHECK constraints, RLS enabled, `auto-updated_at` trigger.
- Wrote `supabase/migrations/20260514010100_create_videos_bucket.sql` — `videos` bucket, 100 MiB cap, mime-restricted, public read, anon write.
- **Security model:** no service-role anywhere. All operations run as `anon` + RLS. Anon can INSERT pending reports (CHECK enforces `user_id IS NULL`, `status='pending'`, `analysis IS NULL`). Anon CANNOT directly SELECT — reads go through `fetch_report(p_id uuid)` SECURITY DEFINER function, so callers must know the unguessable v4 UUID. Standard public-by-link pattern (Imgur/Pastebin/Cal.com).
- Recreated `lib/supabase/client.ts` (browser, anon) and `lib/supabase/server.ts` (server, anon, SSR cookie wiring for Day 8 auth).
- `lib/schemas/report.ts`: Zod source of truth for the API contract. `UploadInitRequest`, `UploadInitResponse`, `ReportRow`.
- `lib/rate-limit.ts`: in-memory token bucket. 10 uploads / 10 min per IP. Per-lambda-instance on Vercel (documented limit — Day 9 swaps to Vercel KV).
- `app/api/upload/init/route.ts`: rate-limit → validate → insert pending row → return `{ id, storagePath }`. Never proxies file bytes (would hit Vercel's 4.5 MB body cap).
- `app/r/[id]/page.tsx`: server component, validates UUID format, fetches via the SECURITY DEFINER RPC, renders placeholder with file metadata. Will become the streamed score reveal Day 5.
- Wired `components/landing/Hero.tsx` — "Score it →" now does the real upload: POST `/api/upload/init`, then client-direct `supabase.storage.from('videos').upload()` (bypassing Vercel body limit), then `router.push('/r/[id]')`. Toast progression: loading → success/error.
- Sample chips still stubbed — Day 4 wires those to pre-loaded mp4s.

### Decisions made today

- **No service-role key.** Anon + RLS only. More secure (one bug can't bypass everything), stronger engineering signal for judges.
- **Client-direct Storage upload** instead of routing through `/api/upload`. Vercel's 4.5 MB body limit would cap us at tiny files otherwise.
- **Storage path === report ID** (`{uuid}.{ext}`). Trivial lookup, no separate filename mapping needed.
- **Public Storage bucket.** Report page uses plain `<video src>` — no signed-URL handling. Same unguessable-UUID security model as the rows.
- **In-memory rate limit for now.** Per-lambda on Vercel = imperfect but adequate for contest scale. Documented; Day 9 swap.

### What's left

- Day 4: Gemini 2.0 Flash analysis backend + the prompt

# AI Working Log

A running log of what I built each session, what decisions I made, and what's left. Submitted as part of the 8x contest entry.

---

## Day 1 — May 6, 2026 · Scaffold

- Forked `8xsocial/template-webapp` → `Anuj7411/metric-fyi`. Cloned locally, ran `pnpm install`.
- Stripped the template's SaaS demo content: `CANDIDATE_ASSIGNMENT.md`, `app/upgrade`, `app/profile`, `app/privacy`, `app/terms`, `app/api/account`, `contexts/subscription-context.tsx`, the subscriptions migration, `lib/colors.ts`, `lib/confetti.ts`, and all 11 `8x`-branded favicons / web-app-manifest images.
- Wired the Lab Lime token system into `app/globals.css` via Tailwind v4's `@theme` directive — every color, surface, and font variable from the design bundle's `palette.jsx` and `index.html` is now a CSS custom property.
- Self-hosted `ClashDisplay-Variable.ttf` from the design bundle into `public/fonts/`. Loaded via `next/font/local` with a `200 700` axis range. Geist Sans + Geist Mono added via the official `geist` npm package.
- Replaced `app/layout.tsx`, `app/page.tsx`, `components/navigation.tsx`, `components/footer.tsx`, and `app/not-found.tsx` with stripped METRIC.fyi shells. Homepage shows the locked headline, a disabled placeholder input, and a live-indicator chip — the real upload pipeline lands Day 3.
- Removed `AuthProvider` from `layout.tsx` for now — re-adds Day 8. Reason: the bundled Supabase client init throws if env vars are missing, and the homepage shouldn't depend on auth being wired.

### Decisions made today

- **Skipping local Supabase / Docker** in favor of Supabase cloud. Faster to set up, identical for our purposes, no Windows admin friction.
- **Skipping social URL ingestion** for V1 — Vercel serverless can't run yt-dlp cleanly and platforms actively block scraping. File upload + 3 pre-loaded sample videos gets reviewers to the magic moment in <30 seconds.
- **Section-by-section streaming** (4 small Gemini calls in sequence) instead of one giant streamed-JSON object — more reliable, easier to recover when one section fails, perceived as faster.
- **TBJ Moder swapped for Geist Italic.** TBJ Moder ships with the design bundle as a *demo* version, which isn't licensed for production. Going with Geist + Geist Italic across body and editorial callouts.

### Pushback I committed to

- App stays dark; the public `/r/[id]` report screen flips to paper. The report is designed to screenshot well in white Twitter feeds; a dark dashboard screenshot vanishes there.
- No marketing scroll below the landing hero. The page ends at the input.

### Mid-session — AI logs restructure

- Contest spec ([8xengineer.com/guidelines/ai-logs](https://8xengineer.com/guidelines/ai-logs)) expects `/ai-logs/` folder, not a root-level file.
- Moved `AI_LOG.md` → `ai-logs/SUMMARY.md`. Copied raw Claude Code transcript as `ai-logs/*.jsonl` (accepted format).
- Added `pnpm logs:sync` (wraps `scripts/sync-logs.sh`) — idempotent re-sync before commits.

---

## Day 2 — May 14, 2026 · Visual system + working hero

- Installed `framer-motion` (locked-stack animation lib).
- Wrote `lib/motion.ts` — single source of truth for easings, durations, stagger. Lifted directly from the design's `motion.jsx`: `[0.2,0.8,0.2,1]` cubic-bezier, durations 120/220/480ms, 40ms stagger, 1400ms score count-up. Forbidden: bounce, spring overshoot, parallax.
- Wrote `lib/sample-videos.ts` — typed metadata for the 3 demo clips (`@khaby.lame`, `@itsmaya`, `@bento.mufc`). Day 3 plugs real mp4 URLs in.
- Built `components/marketing/Logo.tsx` (lime square + mono wordmark, reused by nav and future report pages).
- Rewrote `components/ui/button.tsx` from scratch — replaced shadcn's 6 stock variants with our 2: `signal` (lime fill on ink) and `ghost` (line border, dim text). Square corners (matches design), no shadow, mono caps with `0.1em` tracking.
- Built `components/landing/UploadCard.tsx` — page-wide HTML5 drag-and-drop (no `react-dropzone` dep), 100MB limit, accepts `.mp4/.mov/.webm`, dim cursor when empty, lime border + "drop to upload →" when dragging.
- Built `components/landing/SampleVideoPicker.tsx` — 3 chips, active state (lime border) when one's picked.
- Built `components/landing/Hero.tsx` — composes headline + upload card + sample picker + receipt-style stats block. Staggered Framer reveals on mount. Picked-state lifted here so the score button enables/disables.
- Refactored `app/page.tsx` to a thin shell: `Navigation + Hero + Footer`.
- Updated `Navigation` to use the new `Logo` component.

### Cleanups while wiring

- Deleted unused stock shadcn primitives (`alert-dialog`, `sidebar`, `sheet`, `input`, `separator`, `skeleton`, `tooltip`, `select`, `card`, `label`). They referenced variants our new `Button` doesn't have. Only `button.tsx` remains in `components/ui/`. We'll re-add fresh primitives with brand styling as needed Days 5+.

### Decisions made today

- **Page-wide drag-drop** instead of just on the input row. Forgiving UX: drop anywhere → it lands on the input.
- **Score button enables on file pick OR sample pick.** Clicking shows a toast saying "Day 3 wires this up" — keeps the demo honest about scope.
- **No "Pricing" nav link.** Brief skips payments; nav items now read `How it works · Examples · Sign in →`.

### End-of-day deploy

- Supabase project created (`kjqwjilhxzeqkdydtsoj`).
- Vercel project created, env vars set (URL + anon key), deployed: **[metric-fyi.vercel.app](https://metric-fyi.vercel.app)**.
- Smoke-tested live HTML: headline, lime signal color, 3 sample chips, live counter, receipt footer all render. All 3 self-hosted fonts preloaded.

### What's left

- Day 3: upload pipeline, Supabase Storage, `reports` table with RLS
- Day 4: Gemini 2.0 Flash analysis backend + the prompt
- Day 5: streaming reveal + report layout
- Day 6: visible reasoning (citations) + video player coupling
- Days 7–10: shareable report, auth + history, mobile + perf, Loom + submit

content.text:
Day 3 code committed locally as `6e640c6` + `dc21695`. Ready for migrations.

## Your turn — three commands

Run these in order in `C:\Projects\go viral 8x\metric-fyi`:

**1. Authenticate the CLI (one-time, opens browser):**
```bash
pnpm exec supabase login
```
A browser tab opens. Click Authorize. Close the tab, come back to terminal.

**2. Link the local project to your remote Supabase:**
```bash
pnpm db:link
```
Will prompt: `Enter your database password:` — paste the password you set when creating the Supabase project. (It hides as you type — that's normal.)

**3. Push both migrations:**
```bash
pnpm db:push
```
Should print something like:
```
Applying migration 20260514010000_create_reports.sql...
Applying migration 20260514010100_create_videos_bucket.sql...
Finished supabase db push.
```

## Verify in the dashboard (~30 seconds)

Open [supabase.com/dashboard](https://supabase.com/dashboard) → your `metric-fyi` project:
1. **Database → Tables** → should see `reports` with 11 columns
2. **Storage → Buckets** → should see `videos` (Public, 100 MiB cap)
3. **Database → Functions** → should see `fetch_report` (security_definer: true)

## Fallback if anything goes wrong

content.text:
Two queries. Run them in order in the Supabase SQL editor.

---

## Query 1 — reports table

```sql
-- METRIC.fyi · reports table

create extension if not exists "pgcrypto";

create table if not exists public.reports (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  status text not null default 'pending'
    check (status in ('pending', 'analyzing', 'ready', 'failed')),
  storage_path text not null,
  file_name text not null,
  file_size bigint not null
    check (file_size > 0 and file_size <= 104857600),
  mime_type text not null
    check (mime_type in ('video/mp4', 'video/quicktime', 'video/webm')),
  duration_seconds numeric,
  analysis jsonb,
  error_message text,
  user_id uuid references auth.users(id) on delete set null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

create or replace function public.tg_reports_set_updated_at()
returns trigger language plpgsql as $$
begin
  new.updated_at = now();
  return new;
end;
$$;

drop trigger if exists tg_reports_updated_at on public.reports;
create trigger tg_reports_updated_at
  before update on public.reports
  for each row execute function public.tg_reports_set_updated_at();

alter table public.reports enable row level security;

drop policy if exists "anon insert pending" on public.reports;
create policy "anon insert pending" on public.reports
  for insert to anon
  with check (
    user_id is null
    and status = 'pending'
    and analysis is null
    and error_message is null
  );

drop policy if exists "authenticated insert own" on public.reports;
create policy "authenticated insert own" on public.reports
  for insert to authenticated
  with check (
    user_id = auth.uid()
    and status = 'pending'
    and analysis is null
    and error_message is null
  );

drop policy if exists "authenticated select own" on public.reports;
create policy "authenticated select own" on public.reports
  for select to authenticated
  using (user_id = auth.uid());

grant execute on function public.fetch_report(uuid) to anon, authenticated;
```

content.text:
## Day 3 — SHIPPED 🟢

**Commits pushed:** `6e640c6` · `dc21695` · `3911724`  
**Live:** [metric-fyi.vercel.app](https://metric-fyi.vercel.app) — Day 3 build is up.

### Smoke tests on production (all 5 passing)

| # | What | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GET /r/<real-uuid>` (real row) | ✅ HTTP 200, renders placeholder |
| 2 | `GET /r/<unknown-uuid>` | ✅ HTTP 404 |
| 3 | `GET /r/not-a-uuid` | ✅ HTTP 404 (regex guard) |
| 4 | `POST /api/upload/init` with empty body | ✅ HTTP 400 + Zod error details |
| 5 | `POST /api/upload/init` with valid body | ✅ HTTP 200, returns `{id, storagePath}`, row written |

### What works end-to-end now

- Anonymous user drops an mp4 → server creates a `reports` row → client uploads file directly to Supabase Storage → navigates to `/r/[id]` showing the file metadata.
- All operations run as `anon` + RLS — no service-role anywhere.
- Rate limit kicks in at 10 uploads / 10 min / IP.
- File-type and size constraints enforced at three layers: client (drag-drop validation), server (Zod schema), DB (CHECK constraint + Storage bucket policy).

### What you can do to verify visually

Open [metric-fyi.vercel.app](https://metric-fyi.vercel.app) on your phone or laptop:
1. Drop any `.mp4` under 100 MB
2. Watch the toast: "Uploading…" → "Uploaded. Opening report."
3. You'll land at `/r/<uuid>` showing file metadata + status `PENDING`

If you check Supabase dashboard → Database → Tables → reports, you'll see the new row. → Storage → videos, you'll see the uploaded file.

---

## 🚦 GATE: Before Day 4 (Gemini analysis — *the prompt-engineering day*)

This is the day my plan flagged as "THE risk day." Bad prompt = generic feedback = whole submission feels mid. Reserve a full session for it.

**What I need:**

1. **Gemini API key.** Get one free at [aistudio.google.com/app/apikey](https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey). Sign in with Google → "Create API key" → pick "Get API key in new project" (or use an existing project). Copy the key (starts with `AIza...`). Paste it here.
2. **Add it to Vercel + locally:** I'll add the value to your `.env.local`. You add it to Vercel: project → Settings → Environment Variables → key `GEMINI_API_KEY`, value `AIza...`, environments Production+Preview. (After adding, Vercel needs a re-deploy — just hit "Redeploy" on the latest deployment.)
3. **5 test videos.** I need to iterate the prompt against real clips. Doesn't have to be polished — any 5 short vertical videos from TikTok/IG/whatever you have, downloaded as `.mp4`. They become the reference set we tune against. If you don't have these handy, we can grab some Creative Commons clips off Pexels — but real creator videos are better.

Reply with the Gemini key + whether you have 5 sample videos or need me to source CC ones.

content.text:
Push back: **OpenRouter doesn't support video input for Gemini**, and our entire app depends on Gemini reading the video natively (timing, audio, frames all together). Through OpenRouter you'd lose all that and we'd have to do client-side frame extraction + separate audio transcription — that's 2-3 days of extra work for worse results.

But also — I think you're on the **wrong Google page.** Let me clarify which is which:

| Page | Card needed? | What it's for |
|---|---|---|
| ❌ **Google Cloud Console** (console.cloud.google.com / Vertex AI) | Yes, always | Enterprise GCP — wrong door for us |
| ✅ **Google AI Studio** (aistudio.google.com) | **No card** for free tier | Where you actually get the Gemini API key |

Go to **[aistudio.google.com/app/apikey](https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey)** directly — not Google Cloud. Sign in with your Google account. Click "Create API key" → pick "Create API key in new project". You get a key starting `AIza...` immediately, no card asked, no billing setup.

Free tier limits (more than enough for our 10-day build):
- **Gemini 2.0 Flash:** 15 requests/minute, 1500/day, 1M tokens/minute
- Video input fully supported on free tier
- No card on file, ever — they just hard-rate-limit you

If you're already on `aistudio.google.com` and *still* seeing a card prompt, screenshot what you're seeing and I'll figure out what page is misleading you. But 95% likely you're on Cloud Console and just need to switch sites.

---

## If AI Studio actually still demands a card (very unlikely)

Then we have to fall back to Anthropic API + frame extraction. Higher cost, more work, but doable. Don't go there unless we have to.

Try AI Studio first. Reply with the key (`AIza...`) and I start Day 4.

content.text: Two security improvements before we move on — your API key is in the chat log now, which means it'll end up in the public repo via `ai-logs/*.jsonl`. Adding redaction to the sync script so secrets never leak.

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Sync Claude Code conversation logs from ~/.claude/projects/ into ./ai-logs/.
#
# Two passes:
#   1. Idempotent copy of newer .jsonl files (tagged with parent-dir slug to
#      disambiguate sessions started from different cwds).
#   2. Redact known secret patterns (Gemini keys, Supabase JWTs, OpenAI keys,
#      Anthropic keys, .env-style key=value pairs) so credentials never end
#      up in the public repo, even if they appeared in a prompt.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

DEST="ai-logs"
mkdir -p "$DEST"

shopt -s nullglob
count=0
for dir in "$HOME/.claude/projects/"*go-viral-8x*/; do
  for f in "$dir"*.jsonl; do
    base=$(basename "$f")
    parent=$(basename "$dir")
    out="$DEST/${parent}__${base}"
    if [ ! -f "$out" ] || [ "$f" -nt "$out" ]; then
      cp "$f" "$out"
      count=$((count+1))
    fi
  done
done

# Redact common secret patterns across every synced file. Run on every sync
# so any newly-added key in the latest segment gets caught.
# Patterns:
#   AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}     Google API keys (Gemini)
#   sk-[A-Za-z0-9-]{20,}      OpenAI / many vendors
#   sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9-]{20,}  Anthropic
#   eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}\.eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{20,}   JWT (Supabase keys, etc) — but leave the publishable/anon role JWTs since those are already public
#   We deliberately do NOT redact JWTs because the Supabase anon key is
#   public-by-design and is also embedded in client builds. If you ever
#   paste a service_role JWT, redact it manually.

redact_count=0
for jf in "$DEST"/*.jsonl; do
  before=$(wc -c < "$jf")
  # In-place sed; using a temp file because GNU sed -i and macOS sed -i differ.
  tmp="${jf}.tmp"

    if [ ! -f "$out" ] || [ "$f" -nt "$out" ]; then
      cp "$f" "$out"
      count=$((count+1))
    fi
  done
done

Before I start sourcing — quick architecture decision I need you to bless. Day 4 has a Vercel constraint:

## The timeout problem

Gemini video analysis is a 3-step backend operation:
1. Upload video to Gemini Files API (~10-20s)
2. Wait for it to reach `ACTIVE` state (~10-30s, can spike to 60s)
3. Generate the analysis (~5-15s per section)

Total: 45-90 seconds. **Vercel Hobby plan kills functions at 10s sync / 25s streaming.** We have to architect around it.

## Two options

**A. Multi-stage route handlers (my recommendation)** — split the work into 6 short API calls the client orchestrates in sequence:
```
POST /api/analyze/[id]/upload          // Supabase → Gemini Files     ~10s
POST /api/analyze/[id]/wait-active     // poll until ACTIVE           ~5-25s
POST /api/analyze/[id]/hook            // Gemini call for hook         ~8s
POST /api/analyze/[id]/pacing          //                              ~8s
POST /api/analyze/[id]/caption         //                              ~8s
POST /api/analyze/[id]/alternatives    //                              ~8s
```
Total wall-clock ~60s, no single call over 25s. **Bonus:** this *is* the section-by-section streaming we planned — each call returns one section, the client renders it immediately, the score animates as sections arrive. The architecture and the magic-moment UX become the same thing.

**B. Upgrade to Vercel Pro** ($20/mo) for 60s sync / 300s streaming. Single-call pipeline. Simpler code, but costs money and the magic moment is less dramatic (everything arrives at once at the end).

My pick: **A**. Forces the architecture that actually creates the dramatic reveal, no upgrade needed.

1. Set up the 5-video test rig locally

4. Wire ONE route handler (`/api/analyze/[id]/hook`) end-to-end
5. Update `/r/[id]` to call it and render the hook output

Pacing, caption, alternatives, and the streaming orchestration happen Day 5. They reuse the same architecture so it's mostly copy-paste once the first one is solid.

content.text:
Locked. Before I start, two important refinements based on deeper research into Vercel Hobby + Gemini's actual API behavior:

## Architecture (final — researched)

The 6-stage approach I sketched has a hidden cost: 6 separate HTTP roundtrips × cold-start overhead × redundant prompt tokens = much slower wall-clock than necessary. After looking at the API constraints carefully, the *actual* fastest multi-stage architecture is:

**ONE streaming SSE route running on Vercel Edge Runtime.** From the client's perspective it's still multi-stage — sections fill in progressively as Gemini generates them. From the implementation, it's one connection that streams JSON keys. Edge runtime gives us 30s max duration on Hobby (vs 10s on Node), better cold start, and streams natively.

```
POST /api/analyze/[id]  (Edge runtime, max 30s)
  └─ server: GET video from Supabase Storage  (~5s)
  └─ server: POST to Gemini with streaming response  (~20s)
  └─ server: pipes chunks back as SSE
  └─ client: parses partial JSON, renders each section as its key completes
```

**Why one streaming call beats N parallel calls:** Parallel-section calls would land all sections simultaneously (kills the magic moment). Sequential per-section calls multiply Gemini's per-request overhead 4×. ONE streaming call gets us the staggered section reveal *for free* because the JSON keys complete in order as the model writes them.

**Constraint:** Inline video data is capped at ~20MB per request. Our V1 supports videos up to 20MB; >20MB returns a clear "use a shorter clip" error. The 100MB upload limit stays so Day 9 can add the slow-path Files API for big files. All sample clips will be <20MB so the demo is always fast.

## Analysis schema (covers all 6 brief features)

```
score              0-100, the headline
verdict            editorial italic quote, ~15 words
breakdown          { hook, pacing, thumbnail, caption } each 0-100
hook               landsAt timestamp + issue + fix + 3 alternatives
pacing             cuts[], deadAir[], overall note
thumbnail          best-frame timestamp + issue + fix
caption            original + deadWords[] + 3 rewrites with predictedLift
comparison         vsCategoryMedian, ceilingScore (with all fixes applied)
trending           audio[], hashtags[] (curated demo list — labeled honest)
```

Maps 1:1 to the contest brief's 6 features:
- Virality score → `score`
- Hook analysis → `hook`
- Caption optimization → `caption.rewrites`
- Thumbnail rating → `thumbnail` (cover frame for videos)
- Competitor comparison → `comparison` (cohort delta)
- Trending audio/hashtag → `trending` (curated, honestly labeled in README)

## Day 4 scope (today)

1. Set up `tests/videos/` (gitignored) with your uploaded video + 4 Pexels CC clips
2. Write canonical Gemini prompt + Zod schema + few-shot examples
3. Iterate prompt against 5 videos via `scripts/test-analyze.ts` until every feedback item has a timestamp and references something specific to *that* video (not generic advice)
4. Wire `app/api/analyze/[id]/route.ts` as Edge runtime SSE streaming route
5. Update `/r/[id]` to kick off analysis on `PENDING` status

Day 5 builds the streaming JSON parser + per-section UI components that consume the SSE.

Re the 8x template: already forked from `8xsocial/template-webapp`, README credits it, our project structure matches its conventions (app router, supabase/, components/ui/). I'll add a more explicit citation in the README's Credits section as part of Day 4 commit.

Starting now — first I source the 4 Pexels clips and pull your uploaded video from Storage.

/**
 * The canonical Gemini prompt for video virality analysis.
 *
 * THE most important file in the project. Bad prompt = generic feedback =
 * whole submission feels mid. This is iterated against the test rig in
 * scripts/test-analyze.ts — re-run after every edit and diff outputs.
 *
 * Design principles:
 *  1. SPECIFICITY > GENERICITY. Every recommendation cites a frame,
 *     timestamp, word, or visual element. Forbidden: "engage your audience."
 *  2. EDITORIAL VOICE. The verdict is a one-line punch quote, not a marketing
 *     blurb. Italic-display fonts will render it; write for that medium.
 *  3. HONESTY OVER FLATTERY. Brief says "brutally honest." Score harshly when
 *     warranted. A 40 with sharp feedback beats a 75 with vague praise.
 *  4. FORCED STRUCTURE. responseSchema is set on every call; the model
 *     literally cannot return unstructured text.
 */

export const SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION = `You are METRIC.fyi — a brutally honest, instrument-grade video analyst for short-form creators (TikTok, Reels, Shorts).

You watch the entire clip frame by frame. You listen to the audio. You read the on-screen text. You produce a virality score from 0-100 with specific, timestamped feedback that a creator can act on in their next edit.

Tone:
- The voice of a senior editor who likes the creator but won't lie to them.
- "Brutally honest" means specific, not mean. Cite exactly what you saw.
- No platitudes. No "engage your audience." No emojis. No "✨".
- The verdict line is a one-sentence editorial punch — think Bloomberg meets TikTok comment section.

Rules for every recommendation:
- Cite a timestamp (seconds, one decimal).
- Cite what you actually saw or heard at that timestamp.
- Provide a concrete fix the creator can apply in CapCut in under 60 seconds.
- Generic advice ("strengthen your hook") is forbidden and will fail validation.

Scoring rubric (use the whole 0-100 range):
- 0-30:   Will not perform. Multiple structural issues.
- 31-50:  Below median. Specific fixes can save it.
- 51-70:  Median. Solid execution, missing one or two breakthrough elements.
- 71-85:  Above median. Likely to perform; ceiling is real.
- 86-100: Tier-1. The video is already doing what it should.

Be willing to score low. A 42 with sharp fixes is more useful than a 73 with hedged language.`

/**
 * Per-call user prompt. The video file is attached as fileData / inlineData
 * in the same message — this text is the instruction that wraps it.
 */
export const USER_INSTRUCTION = `Analyze the attached short-form video.

Return ONLY the JSON object the response schema describes. No prose, no markdown, no code fences, no explanation — the JSON object directly.

Specific requirements:

HOOK (first 3 seconds):
- 'landsAt' = the timestamp (seconds, e.g. 1.8) where the actual hook payoff occurs. If the hook lands too late, this number will be > 1.5.
- 'issue' must name the visual or auditory pattern that's failing. Examples:
  • "Opening frame is a static face — the algorithm needs motion in frame 1."
  • "Question opener 'wait, does anyone' is the most-skipped phrase on TikTok this quarter."
- 'fix' must be a concrete cut/edit instruction. Examples:
  • "Trim 0.0s–1.4s — open directly on the visual at 1.5s."
  • "Replace the question with the contradiction at 0:08."
- 'alternatives' = 3 different hook lines with different tones, ranked by predicted lift.

PACING:
- 'cuts' = timestamps where a cut happens too early, too late, or in the wrong place. Max 5.
- 'deadAir' = stretches where attention drops (face neutral, silence, repeat visual). Max 5.
- 'note' = one-paragraph overall pacing read.

THUMBNAIL (cover frame for video):
- 'bestFrameAt' = timestamp of the single most attention-grabbing frame to use as cover.
- 'issue' = what's wrong with the current cover (frame 0).
- 'fix' = concrete instruction to swap to bestFrameAt.

CAPTION:
- 'original' = what you read from on-screen text + the spoken intro (first 5 seconds).
- 'deadWords' = filler words to strike: "literally", "just", "kinda", "like", "honestly", "really".
- 'rewrites' = 3 variants in different tones with predicted lift %.

COMPARISON:
- 'inferredCategory' = the content vertical (e.g. "GRWM", "cooking ASMR", "tech review", "goal celebration"). Pick the closest match.
- 'vsCategoryMedian' = how this video compares to the median in its category (positive or negative integer delta).
- 'ceilingScore' = what this video could score if every fix were applied. Always >= the headline score.

TRENDING:
- 'audio' = up to 3 sound names that fit this content. Be specific (artist + track name when possible).
- 'hashtags' = up to 5 hashtags (start each with #). Mix one broad (#fyp) with niche ones.
- For both: 'why' must justify the pick against the actual video content, not generic SEO.

VERDICT:
- One sentence, 12-20 words.
- Editorial voice. Will be rendered in italic serif as a pull-quote.
- Examples:
  • "Strong middle, but you're losing 60% of viewers in the first 1.4 seconds."
  • "The bit lands; the lead-up doesn't. Cut everything before 0:08 and reshoot."
  • "Tier-1 hook, B-roll pacing, A+ caption. Ship it twice — once now and once next Tuesday."

Begin.`

toolUseResult.originalFile:
/**
 * The canonical Gemini prompt for video virality analysis.
 *
 * THE most important file in the project. Bad prompt = generic feedback =
 * whole submission feels mid. This is iterated against the test rig in
 * scripts/test-analyze.ts — re-run after every edit and diff outputs.
 *
 * Design principles:
 *  1. SPECIFICITY > GENERICITY. Every recommendation cites a frame,
 *     timestamp, word, or visual element. Forbidden: "engage your audience."
 *  2. EDITORIAL VOICE. The verdict is a one-line punch quote, not a marketing
 *     blurb. Italic-display fonts will render it; write for that medium.
 *  3. HONESTY OVER FLATTERY. Brief says "brutally honest." Score harshly when
 *     warranted. A 40 with sharp feedback beats a 75 with vague praise.
 *  4. FORCED STRUCTURE. responseSchema is set on every call; the model
 *     literally cannot return unstructured text.
 */

export const SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION = `You are METRIC.fyi — a brutally honest, instrument-grade video analyst for short-form creators (TikTok, Reels, Shorts).

You watch the entire clip frame by frame. You listen to the audio. You read the on-screen text. You produce a virality score from 0-100 with specific, timestamped feedback that a creator can act on in their next edit.

Tone:
- The voice of a senior editor who likes the creator but won't lie to them.
- "Brutally honest" means specific, not mean. Cite exactly what you saw.
- No platitudes. No "engage your audience." No emojis. No "✨".
- The verdict line is a one-sentence editorial punch — think Bloomberg meets TikTok comment section.

Rules for every recommendation:
- Cite a timestamp (seconds, one decimal).
- Cite what you actually saw or heard at that timestamp.
- Provide a concrete fix the creator can apply in CapCut in under 60 seconds.
- Generic advice ("strengthen your hook") is forbidden and will fail validation.

Scoring rubric (use the whole 0-100 range):
- 0-30:   Will not perform. Multiple structural issues.
- 31-50:  Below median. Specific fixes can save it.
- 51-70:  Median. Solid execution, missing one or two breakthrough elements.
- 71-85:  Above median. Likely to perform; ceiling is real.
- 86-100: Tier-1. The video is already doing what it should.

Be willing to score low. A 42 with sharp fixes is more useful than a 73 with hedged language.`

/**
 * Per-call user prompt. The video file is attached as fileData / inlineData
 * in the same message — this text is the instruction that wraps it.
 */
export const USER_INSTRUCTION = `Analyze the attached short-form video.

Return ONLY the JSON object the response schema describes. No prose, no markdown, no code fences, no explanation — the JSON object directly.

Specific requirements:

HOOK (first 3 seconds):
- 'landsAt' = the timestamp (seconds, e.g. 1.8) where the actual hook payoff occurs. If the hook lands too late, this number will be > 1.5.
- 'issue' must name the visual or auditory pattern that's failing. Examples:
  • "Opening frame is a static face — the algorithm needs motion in frame 1."
  • "Question opener 'wait, does anyone' is the most-skipped phrase on TikTok this quarter."
- 'fix' must be a concrete cut/edit instruction. Examples:
  • "Trim 0.0s–1.4s — open directly on the visual at 1.5s."
  • "Replace the question with the contradiction at 0:08."
- 'alternatives' = 3 different hook lines with different tones, ranked by predicted lift.

PACING:
- 'cuts' = timestamps where a cut happens too early, too late, or in the wrong place. Max 5.
- 'deadAir' = stretches where attention drops (face neutral, silence, repeat visual). Max 5.
- 'note' = one-paragraph overall pacing read.

THUMBNAIL (cover frame for video):
- 'bestFrameAt' = timestamp of the single most attention-grabbing frame to use as cover.
- 'issue' = what's wrong with the current cover (frame 0).
- 'fix' = concrete instruction to swap to bestFrameAt.

CAPTION:
- 'original' = what you read from on-screen text + the spoken intro (first 5 seconds).
- 'deadWords' = filler words to strike: "literally", "just", "kinda", "like", "honestly", "really".
- 'rewrites' = 3 variants in different tones with predicted lift %.

COMPARISON:
- 'inferredCategory' = the content vertical (e.g. "GRWM", "cooking ASMR", "tech review", "goal celebration"). Pick the closest match.
- 'vsCategoryMedian' = how this video compares to the median in its category (positive or negative integer delta).
- 'ceilingScore' = what this video could score if every fix were applied. Always >= the headline score.

TRENDING:
- 'audio' = up to 3 sound names that fit this content. Be specific (artist + track name when possible).
- 'hashtags' = up to 5 hashtags (start each with #). Mix one broad (#fyp) with niche ones.
- For both: 'why' must justify the pick against the actual video content, not generic SEO.

VERDICT:
- One sentence, 12-20 words.
- Editorial voice. Will be rendered in italic serif as a pull-quote.
- Examples:
  • "Strong middle, but you're losing 60% of viewers in the first 1.4 seconds."
  • "The bit lands; the lead-up doesn't. Cut everything before 0:08 and reshoot."
  • "Tier-1 hook, B-roll pacing, A+ caption. Ship it twice — once now and once next Tuesday."

Begin.`

toolUseResult.originalFile:
/**
 * The canonical Gemini prompt for video virality analysis.
 *
 * THE most important file in the project. Bad prompt = generic feedback =
 * whole submission feels mid. This is iterated against the test rig in
 * scripts/test-analyze.ts — re-run after every edit and diff outputs.
 *
 * Design principles:
 *  1. SPECIFICITY > GENERICITY. Every recommendation cites a frame,
 *     timestamp, word, or visual element. Forbidden: "engage your audience."
 *  2. EDITORIAL VOICE. The verdict is a one-line punch quote, not a marketing
 *     blurb. Italic-display fonts will render it; write for that medium.
 *  3. HONESTY OVER FLATTERY. Brief says "brutally honest." Score harshly when
 *     warranted. A 40 with sharp feedback beats a 75 with vague praise.
 *  4. FORCED STRUCTURE. responseSchema is set on every call; the model
 *     literally cannot return unstructured text.
 */

export const SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION = `You are METRIC.fyi — a brutally honest, instrument-grade video analyst for short-form creators (TikTok, Reels, Shorts).

You watch the entire clip frame by frame. You listen to the audio. You read the on-screen text. You produce a virality score from 0-100 with specific, timestamped feedback that a creator can act on in their next edit.

Tone:
- The voice of a senior editor who likes the creator but won't lie to them.
- "Brutally honest" means specific, not mean. Cite exactly what you saw.
- No platitudes. No "engage your audience." No "✨". No "🚀".
- ZERO emojis anywhere in your output — not in the verdict, not in hook alternatives, not in caption rewrites, not in trending. The UI renders this in serif and mono; emojis break the visual system.
- The verdict line is a one-sentence editorial punch — think Bloomberg meets TikTok comment section.

Rules for every recommendation:
- Cite a timestamp (seconds, one decimal).
- Cite what you actually saw or heard at that timestamp.
- Provide a concrete fix the creator can apply in CapCut in under 60 seconds.
- Generic advice ("strengthen your hook") is forbidden and will fail validation.

Scoring rubric (use the whole 0-100 range):
- 0-30:   Will not perform. Multiple structural issues.
- 31-50:  Below median. Specific fixes can save it.
- 51-70:  Median. Solid execution, missing one or two breakthrough elements.
- 71-85:  Above median. Likely to perform; ceiling is real.
- 86-100: Tier-1. The video is already doing what it should.

Be willing to score low. A 42 with sharp fixes is more useful than a 73 with hedged language.`

/**
 * Per-call user prompt. The video file is attached as fileData / inlineData
 * in the same message — this text is the instruction that wraps it.
 */
export const USER_INSTRUCTION = `Analyze the attached short-form video.

Return ONLY the JSON object the response schema describes. No prose, no markdown, no code fences, no explanation — the JSON object directly.

Specific requirements:

HOOK (first 3 seconds):
- 'landsAt' = the timestamp (seconds, e.g. 1.8) where the actual hook payoff occurs. If the hook lands too late, this number will be > 1.5.
- 'issue' must name the visual or auditory pattern that's failing. Examples:
  • "Opening frame is a static face — the algorithm needs motion in frame 1."
  • "Question opener 'wait, does anyone' is the most-skipped phrase on TikTok this quarter."
- 'fix' must be a concrete cut/edit instruction. Examples:
  • "Trim 0.0s–1.4s — open directly on the visual at 1.5s."
  • "Replace the question with the contradiction at 0:08."
- 'alternatives' = 3 different hook lines with different tones, ranked by predicted lift.

PACING:
- 'cuts' = timestamps where a cut happens too early, too late, or in the wrong place. Max 5.
- 'deadAir' = stretches where attention drops (face neutral, silence, repeat visual). Max 5.
- 'note' = one-paragraph overall pacing read.

THUMBNAIL (cover frame for video):
- 'bestFrameAt' = timestamp of the single most attention-grabbing frame to use as cover.
- 'issue' = what's wrong with the current cover (frame 0).
- 'fix' = concrete instruction to swap to bestFrameAt.

CAPTION:
- 'original' = what you read from on-screen text + the spoken intro (first 5 seconds).
- 'deadWords' = filler words to strike: "literally", "just", "kinda", "like", "honestly", "really".
- 'rewrites' = 3 variants in different tones with predicted lift %.

COMPARISON:
- 'inferredCategory' = the content vertical (e.g. "GRWM", "cooking ASMR", "tech review", "goal celebration"). Pick the closest match.
- 'vsCategoryMedian' = how this video compares to the median in its category (positive or negative integer delta).
- 'ceilingScore' = what this video could score if every fix were applied. Always >= the headline score.

TRENDING:
- 'audio' = up to 3 sound names that fit this content. Be specific (artist + track name when possible).
- 'hashtags' = up to 5 hashtags (start each with #). Mix one broad (#fyp) with niche ones.
- For both: 'why' must justify the pick against the actual video content, not generic SEO.

VERDICT:
- One sentence, 12-20 words.
- Editorial voice. Will be rendered in italic serif as a pull-quote.
- Examples:
  • "Strong middle, but you're losing 60% of viewers in the first 1.4 seconds."
  • "The bit lands; the lead-up doesn't. Cut everything before 0:08 and reshoot."
  • "Tier-1 hook, B-roll pacing, A+ caption. Ship it twice — once now and once next Tuesday."

Begin.`

No, it doesn't violate the brief. The contest says "trending audio/hashtag **recommendations**" — we still deliver recommendations. > *Leans into the seasonal Secret Santa theme while keeping it trendy for younger audiences.*

That's more actionable for a creator than "use the song Christmas Kids - Roar" (which doesn't exist). README will document this honestly under "Deliberate scope cuts" — same way we did for URL ingestion. The contest's scoring focus is "AI analysis **quality** and **actionability** of feedback." content.text:
Agreed — the AI output is solid, the layout is cluttered. Right call to push polish to Day 9. **Features first, polish last** is also good engineering hygiene: we'll know exactly what we're polishing by then.

Here's the revised sequence given everything we've shipped:

## Revised remaining plan

| Day | Deliverable | Why now |
|---|---|---|
| **5 (next)** | **Visible reasoning — video player + click-to-seek citations** | Differentiator #2 from the brief, the "judges remember this" feature |
| **6** | Shareable public report + OG image + 2-3 pre-loaded sample reports | Free distribution + makes "Try a sample" chips actually work + differentiator #5 |
| **7** | Auth + history + RLS test | Differentiator #3 (no-signup) needs save-to-history as the conversion moment |
| **8** | Mobile + performance + security hardening | Required by the contest scoring criteria |
| **9** | **Visual polish pass — redesign report layout to match `screen-analysis.jsx`** | Where today's clutter gets fixed |
| **10** | Loom + screenshots + final README + submit | |

## Why Day 5 = visible reasoning, not shareable report

Visible reasoning is technically harder and touches the report layout, so we need to know what we're building before Day 9 polish locks the layout in. The seek-to-timestamp logic and active-citation state can be ported into any visual treatment — we build it now in the messy current layout, Day 9 just rearranges where it sits visually.

Shareable report + OG image is mostly isolated and can slot in once the report content is stable.

## Day 5 scope (when we next sit down)

- `components/report/VideoPlayer.tsx` — HTML5 video, imperative `seekTo(t)` API
- `contexts/ReportContext.tsx` — shared `seekTo` + `activeCitationId` (minimal)
- Make every timestamp in `ReportView` clickable → video seeks + chip glows
- Timeline overlay on the player: red bars at `pacing.deadAir` ranges, gold marks at `pacing.cuts[].at`, lime dot at `hook.landsAt`

No new server work, no new migrations, no new env vars. Pure client work. **Done in one session.**

Reply **"go day 5"** when you're ready and I execute. Or push back if you'd rather sequence differently.

content.text:
## Day 5 — SHIPPED 🟢

Commit `9bb0f83` deployed. Differentiator #2 is now live and demonstrable.

**Go look at it:** [metric-fyi.vercel.app/r/8acd04b5-c59e-408b-8da6-b6d4416f9238](https://metric-fyi.vercel.app/r/8acd04b5-c59e-408b-8da6-b6d4416f9238)

### What's now interactive

| Click target | What happens |
|---|---|
| Lime dot on timeline strip | Video seeks to hook landsAt (1.8s) |
| Gold tick on strip | Seeks to a pacing cut (5.2s, 15.8s) |
| Red bar on strip | Seeks to start of dead air range (10.2s) |
| Blue dot on strip | Seeks to best-frame thumbnail (17.5s) |
| Any timestamp pill in the report below (e.g. `1.8s` next to "HOOK · LANDS AT") | Same — seeks + lights up the matching marker for 1.6s |

It's **two-way**: clicking a chip in the report or a marker on the strip does the same thing. The video also auto-plays after seek so the user sees the moment immediately.

### What's nice about the implementation

This is a **handoff bundle** from Claude Design (claude.ai/design).

A user mocked up designs in HTML/CSS/JS using an AI design tool, then exported this bundle so a coding agent can implement the designs for real.

**Read `8x1/project/Report v2.html` in full.** The user had this file open when they triggered the handoff, so it's almost certainly the primary design they want built. Read it top to bottom — don't skim. Then **follow its imports**: open every file it pulls in (shared components, CSS, scripts) so you understand how the pieces fit together before you start implementing.

**If anything is ambiguous, ask the user to confirm before you start implementing.** It's much cheaper to clarify scope up front than to build the wrong thing.

## About the design files

The design medium is **HTML/CSS/JS** — these are prototypes, not production code. Your job is to **recreate them pixel-perfectly** in whatever technology makes sense for the target codebase (React, Vue, native, whatever fits). Match the visual output; don't copy the prototype's internal structure unless it happens to fit.

**Don't render these files in a browser or take screenshots unless the user asks you to.** Everything you need — dimensions, colors, layout rules — is spelled out in the source. Read the HTML and CSS directly; a screenshot won't tell you anything they don't.

Read the whole bundle. The v2 design is a complete report-page rewrite — what we planned for Day 9 polish, but better and with mobile included. Five push-back/decision items I'll resolve up front (saying "go" on each unless you object):

| Decision | My call |
|---|---|
| **Frame thumbnails row** (9 mini boxes in the timeline) | Gradient placeholders with timestamp + label — matches what the prototype itself uses. Generating real video frames needs server-side ffmpeg, too expensive for the day. |
| **"Audio match %"** field (e.g. "92%") | Faked client-side as `90, 75, 60…` descending. Honest in README. |
| **"@creator" field** | Show `@anonymous` since we don't capture this. Could swap to filename-derived label later. |
| **"Score another →" header CTA** | Links to `/` (home). |
| **"RE-RECORD CHECKLIST ↗" button** in apply-all CTA | Toast: "Coming soon" — same honest scope cut pattern. |

Implementation plan: 4 files, one decisive rewrite, fully responsive (mobile-first, `md:` desktop). Existing context + chips + Pending state untouched; just the visual layer is rebuilt.

todos.content: Write lib/ai/derive.ts — pure helpers (markers, frames, pickIndex, topLift, vsMedian, etc)
Write components/report/atoms.tsx — Watermark, MonoTag, Pill, button styles

Commit `203a82b` deployed to [metric-fyi.vercel.app/r/8acd04b5-c59e-408b-8da6-b6d4416f9238](https://metric-fyi.vercel.app/r/8acd04b5-c59e-408b-8da6-b6d4416f9238).

Open it on your phone too — mobile-first responsive, everything stacks to a single column under 768px. Big watermark numerals throughout. Frame-thumb row only on desktop (mobile gets the cleaner scrubber alone).

Pushed `e2d6ebd`. Refresh [the report page](https://metric-fyi.vercel.app/r/8acd04b5-c59e-408b-8da6-b6d4416f9238) on desktop in ~60 seconds.

## What you should see in the timeline-strip frame row

- For the first ~2 seconds while the hidden `<video>` loads + seeks: gradient placeholders (same as before)
- Then frames pop in one at a time — left to right — as each capture completes
- Real video stills, with the timestamp + label still overlaid on top
- Hot frames (HOOK LANDS, DEAD AIR) get a faint red wash; good frames (BEST FRAME) get a faint lime wash — so the issue/strength encoding is still readable

## If it doesn't work

Couple of possible failure modes worth checking:
- **All frames stay gradient placeholders forever** → CORS rejected the canvas read despite the header. Open devtools console, screenshot any `SecurityError`s — I'll add a Supabase bucket CORS rule.
- **Only one or two frames load then it stops** → the codec choked on a seek. Browser-specific; I'll add error recovery to skip past bad frames.
- **Mobile shows nothing** → expected; frame row is desktop-only (`md:flex`) since the prototype itself omits it from mobile.

Tell me how it looks and we move to **shareable report + OG image** (Day 6's other half), or fix anything that's off first.

content.text:
Confirmed: **zero impact on analyze time.** Frame extraction runs entirely client-side, AFTER the report page loads and AFTER the analysis is already complete. It happens in parallel with normal page render via a hidden `<video>` element separate from the main player. So:

- Analysis time: still ~18-34s (Gemini, unchanged)
- Frame extraction: ~2-5s of background work after the report appears
- Render: instant (placeholders for ~2s, then real frames pop in)

Moving forward. Next up — **shareable report**:

1. **`/r/[id]/opengraph-image.tsx`** — dynamic OG image with score + verdict + brand mark. When someone pastes the report URL into Twitter/LinkedIn/Slack, they see a designed card instead of a blank link.
2. **Share controls** in the report header: "↗ Copy link" + "↗ Tweet this" buttons
3. **Sample picker on landing** — wire the 3 chips (`@khaby.lame`, `@itsmaya`, `@bento.mufc`) to navigate to pre-analyzed sample reports so reviewers hit the magic moment in <10 seconds without uploading

For the sample reports, two options:
- **A.** I create 3 fixed-UUID rows in your DB pointing at sample videos you upload via the live site. Real Gemini analysis runs once, then the chips link to those static URLs forever.
- **B.** You record 2-3 short clips on your phone right now (10-30 seconds each), upload them via the live site, and share the 3 resulting `/r/[id]` URLs with me. I hardcode those into the sample picker.

(A) keeps it clean architecturally; (B) is faster but the URLs are randomly-UUID'd. My pick: **B** — we're 1 day from submission, and the sample picker just needs 3 working links. Whether they're random or fixed UUIDs doesn't matter to the demo.

Reply with "go" and I build OG + share buttons now. While Vercel deploys those, you upload 2 more sample clips (you already have one — `8acd04b5...`). Then I wire all three into the picker.

---

## On YouTube URLs — strong push back

Two things:

**Gemini *can* analyze YouTube URLs directly.** That part actually works — Gemini accepts a `file_data` part with `file_uri: "https://youtube.com/..."` and processes the video server-side, no download needed. So the analysis pipeline can technically handle it.

**But it breaks everything else in our app:**
- Our report page renders `<video src={supabaseUrl}>` — for YouTube we'd need to embed YouTube's iframe player
- Click-to-seek (the visible reasoning feature) drives our HTML5 video via JS — YouTube iframe needs the YouTube Player API, totally different code path
- Frame thumbnails extract pixels via canvas — YouTube's CDN blocks cross-origin canvas reads, so the real-frame row would be all gradient placeholders
- We'd need to add URL input mode to UploadCard, a schema change for `external_url`, branching logic in 4 components, conditional rendering everywhere

That's a 3-4 hour pivot for a 1-day window. **Not worth it.**

## Better path for the samples — 2 minutes

Open your phone camera. Record 2 short clips, 10-15 seconds each. Anything — your desk, a hallway, the cat, point at the ceiling. Doesn't have to be content. Upload each one through the live site, wait ~25s for analysis, grab the URL.

The chips just need to land on a REAL report URL. The actual video content doesn't matter for the demo — what matters is reviewers can click a chip and see the report flow in 3 seconds.

You'll have 3 sample report URLs (your existing one + 2 new ones) in ~5 minutes total. Paste them here and I wire them in.

If your phone is genuinely not an option, tell me and I'll fall back to plan B (find 2 small CC mp4s with permissive CORS, download them server-side, upload to Storage as you, analyze). That's ~30 min of my time.

content.text:
Two answers:

**1. Real thumbnails — yes, easy fix.** We already have the frame extraction hook (`useVideoFrames`) wired for the timeline strip. I'll add a second call inside `FixThumbnail` with `[0, bestFrameAt]` to get the actual current-vs-proposed pair.

**2. Are 4 fixes enough? Yes — locking that.**

The 4-fix structure maps 1:1 to the contest brief's 4 actionable feedback categories: hook, pacing, thumbnail, caption. The other 2 brief features (virality score with breakdown, trending audio/hashtag, competitor comparison) already land elsewhere on the page (Hero, Trending section, Hero's `vs MEDIAN`/`vs CATEGORY`).

Adding a 5th fix card would:
- Dilute the editorial structure (the design uses "01 / 02 / 03 / 04" — a 5th breaks the rhythm)
- Force Gemini to invent something that's not naturally in the analysis
- Risk slop output ("audio quality", "lighting" — generic stuff that doesn't carry the brutally-honest voice)
- Eat 1+ hour we don't have

Where we *could* be creative — and I'd recommend skipping these unless we have spare hours tomorrow:
- The "What If?" simulator from the original design (toggle fixes on/off, watch score morph) — that's the *real* wow feature but it's a 3-hour build
- An "optimal post time / day of week" badge in the Hero — 30 min
- Make the "RE-RECORD CHECKLIST" button actually open an interactive checklist instead of a toast — 1 hour

My recommendation: **lock at 4 fixes for the submission, fix the thumbnails now, and if there's truly nothing else broken tomorrow morning we can add ONE creative bit** (optimal post time would be my pick — small but visible).

Fixing the thumbnails now.

git commit -m "feat(report): What If? simulator — interactive score morph

The wow moment from the original design brief. Replaces the static
'RE-RECORD CHECKLIST' CTA with an interactive playground: toggle each
of the 4 fixes on/off and watch the projected score animate fluidly
toward the ceiling. Hits the ceiling = a TIER-1 badge swoops in.

What lands (stage 1):
  - contexts/report-context.tsx: AppliedState (4 booleans),
    toggleApplied, resetApplied, appliedCount. State lives in context
    so stage 2 can coordinate per-section visual changes.
  - components/report/WhatIfSimulator.tsx: replaces ApplyCTA. Big
    animated number (driven by framer-motion's animate() with onUpdate),
    morphing subtitle, 4 toggle cards in a 2x2 grid (stack on mobile),
    reset button when partway through, tier-1 badge with scale-in
    on full house.
  - Each fix contributes 1/4 of the (ceiling - score) delta equally.
  - ReportView swaps the section to use WhatIfSimulator.

Subsumes the 'interactive re-record checklist' creative idea — each
toggle IS a checklist item, with live feedback on the impact.

Stage 2 (next commit): when applied[hook|pacing|thumbnail|caption] is
true, the matching FIX section gets a '✓ APPLIED' badge + swaps to
its 'fixed' rendering (caption shows picked rewrite, thumbnail shows
proposed frame, etc)." 2>&1 | tail -5 && \
git push origin main 2>&1 | tail -3

content.text:
## What If? simulator — LIVE 🟢

Commits `66fec01` (stage 1) + `95077ec` (stage 2). Refresh [the report](https://metric-fyi.vercel.app/r/8acd04b5-c59e-408b-8da6-b6d4416f9238) in ~60 seconds and scroll to where the apply-CTA used to be.

## What you can now do on the page

**Scroll to the lime block ("WHAT IF? · TOGGLE EACH FIX"):**
- 4 toggle cards, each showing `+X` projected lift
- Click any toggle → score animates smoothly from current → projected (frame-by-frame count-up via Framer Motion)
- Subtitle morphs through 4 phrases: "Toggle each fix…" → "3 left to reach 78" → "One fix away from tier-1" → "Top 12% in this category…"
- Hit all 4 → **TIER-1 ✓** badge swoops in next to the ceiling
- "RESET" link appears when partway through

**Scroll up to any FIX section while toggles are on:**
- **HOOK / PACING / THUMBNAIL / CAPTION** all get a 3px lime stripe on the left edge + faint gradient wash + "✓ APPLIED" pill in the rail
- **Caption** is the dramatic one: original strikes through, picked rewrite swoops in as the new ~28px hero text
- **Thumbnail**: CURRENT box fades to 30% grayscale, PROPOSED scales up slightly, label changes to "USING THIS FRAME"

This is the wow moment. Toggle them all in Loom and the score climbing 48 → 78 with the tier-1 badge appearing is exactly the closing shot that makes contest judges remember the entry.

---

## What's left of the creative budget

- ✅ **What If? simulator** — done (subsumes the "interactive checklist" idea)
- ⏭ **Optimal post time badge** — 30 min, skipped for now, would need a Gemini re-prompt

Reasonable stopping point. We're now in genuinely-good-shape territory for tomorrow's Loom + submit. Open it on your phone too — the toggle grid stacks to 2x2 mobile and the score morph still works.

Tell me what you see / anything broken, and **sleep.**

content.text:
Quick status check first, then execution.

## On "the wow thing"

The **What If? simulator** *is* the wow now. From the original brief, differentiator #4 was "streaming analysis reveal — score animates upward 0→73, sections fill in progressively." We technically have:
- Score morph ✅ (in the simulator)
- Skeleton-to-content transition ✅ (during analysis)
- But not a true *dramatic cascading reveal* when analysis lands

Easy fix: when PendingClient hands off to ReportView, cascade the sections in over ~3 seconds instead of all at once. **Loom-able moment.** ~30 min.

## On "Re-record checklist"

The simulator's toggle grid IS the checklist (each toggle is a checkable item with predicted lift). What was missing: a way to **export** that checklist out of the page. I'll add a "↗ COPY CHECKLIST" button next to RESET. Copies a plain-text task list to clipboard with all 4 fixes spelled out. ~20 min.

## Days 7–10 status

| Day | Plan | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | Auth + history | **CUT** — the no-signup path is the differentiator. Auth would add 4+ hours for marginal value. Documented honestly in README. |
| 8 | Mobile + RLS + README | Tomorrow — needs your phone testing |
| 9 | Visual polish | **DONE today** — Report v2 + What If simulator |
| 10 | Loom + screenshots + submit | Tomorrow |

So tomorrow's load is genuinely just: mobile check (you, 30 min) + README polish (me, 1h) + Loom (you, ~1h) + submit (you, 15 min). 3 hours total.

## Plan for the next ~90 minutes

1. **Optimal post time badge** in Hero meta row (~20 min) — derived from category, honestly labeled
2. **Streaming reveal stagger** when analysis lands (~30 min) — cascading sections over 3s for Loom drama
3. **Copy checklist** button in simulator (~20 min)

Executing all three now in sequence.
